findings.description: When the copy pass times out, the fallback runs a fresh `-M -l0` rename pass instead of reusing the one diff-size makes, as the JSDoc and ADR 0145 L24 say it does. A session that forces the timeout makes the gate run git's unbounded rename matching twice under the merge lock, on top of the 30 s copy pass.

The JSDoc `Decision points in one file — the gate compares deltas, so the absolute scale is free.` is now false: COMPLEXITY_NEW_FILE_FLAG_CAP (50) reads the absolute count for new files. ADR 0145 calls this owed, but a one-line reword here would close it.

The copy pass can block the merge lock for up to 30 s. It runs synchronously before the build, so a gate whose build fails still pays for it. Its time also appears in no stage's `elapsedMs`, because `complexityStarted` is taken about 120 lines later.

The copy-pairing deadline is wall-clock, so machine load can flip the complexity verdict on the same branch: a copy of a 60-point file grown to 62 passes when paired (+2) but flags when the pass times out (62 > 50), and a copy of a 10-point file grown to 45 goes the other way.

The comment `// A renamed or copied file is judged against its source (decision 145).` repeats what the `complexitySources` JSDoc and the `GateDebtMeasurement.complexity` JSDoc already say (general.md §Comments seam-duplication test); delete it.

judgeComplexity's map builds `{file, points, limit, label}` with a pre-formatted display `label`, mixing judging with presentation, and chains a nested `before.get(f.file) ?? (source === undefined ? undefined : before.get(source))` lookup; deriving the label at the quoting site would flatten it.

`RawDiffEntry` gains `copiedFrom` alongside `renamedFrom`, but its only reader (`complexitySources`) immediately merges them with `renamedFrom ?? copiedFrom`; diff-size reads only `renamedFrom`, so the split carries no information either caller uses.

`sources` and `copiesPaired` always travel together (returned by `complexitySources`, rebuilt as `{ sources: {}, copiesPaired: true }` in measureBranch, stored on `GateDebtMeasurement.complexity`); a data clump that an ad-hoc shape repeats in three places.
ADR 0145 lines 28 and 78 overrun the file's wrap width, and line 78 folds an unrelated docs/04 remark into the backlog sentence about t-mvv19qls; give it its own sentence.

The PR body says the rule is shared 'in one module that init and the gate both read', but init reads no complexity rule; only debt.service.ts and merge-gate.service.ts use the constants. No code is duplicated, so drop the claim from the PR body.
